description: Event-bus performance budget baseline (D4 / shared invariant 15). NOTE ON WHY THIS FILE IS SMALL: the reason for moving onto the event bus is NOT speed — it is auditability, record+replay, and observability (every event can flow through the bus capture/tap). Performance is only a guardrail: the bus must not be so slow that it regresses a hot path toward milliseconds. So this file commits absolute speed guardrails, not a performance case for the migration. Each metric is an ABSOLUTE ceiling plus, where a migration made one load-bearing, a CORRECTNESS invariant — not a regression comparison against a pre-migration baseline. What matters for a migrated module is that it WORKS CORRECTLY and that its bus path is a REASONABLE ABSOLUTE SPEED; how it compares to the old in-process call is not the budget. 'Reasonable' has a concrete bar: sub-millisecond is fine — nanoseconds to low microseconds is perfectly acceptable, and a ceiling only exists to catch a gross regression that would push the bus toward milliseconds (e.g. a per-event syscall, or an async publish silently becoming synchronous). Both ceilings below are one microsecond with headroom over the observed values. scripts/check_bus_perf_gate.sh enforces these as a merge gate, and changing a ceiling is a reviewed change to this file so 'within budget' always names a real, checkable number.

dispatch_overhead_ns.description: Per-event bus dispatch: host enqueue (a producer writing its outbound ring) through client dequeue (a subscriber reading its inbound ring), excluding module work on the payload. Median over batched samples from src/tests/bus_bench.c.
dispatch_overhead_ns.observed_note: reference dev box, 16-byte inline payload; the ceiling carries ~7x headroom so CI variance does not flake the gate while a gross regression (e.g. a per-event syscall) still trips it.

audit_enqueue_overhead_ns.description: Caller-side cost of publishing one governed-action audit row over the bus (audit_bus_emit), EXCLUDING the ledger write, which the migration moves off the caller's thread. This is the committed budget shape for the first real migration (delivery step 3), which is asynchronous: for an async publish the number that matters is what it costs the caller, not a request/reply round trip. Each test_bus_audit_durability run reports the median of 5,000 per-emit samples; observed_ns is the median of eight controlled per-run medians.
audit_enqueue_overhead_ns.observed_note: 2026-08-26 controlled reference on an Intel i7-14700K with the test pinned to CPU 1: eight per-run medians were 119, 121, 119, 115, 121, 115, 115, and 115 ns (range 115-121 ns; median 117 ns). The ceiling carries ~8x headroom while a gross regression (a per-emit syscall, or the async being lost so the caller waits on the write) still trips the gate.

audit_durability.description: The audit migration is all-or-nothing: the direct write is gone, so every row the bus accepts MUST reach the ledger exactly once, and a graceful shutdown MUST drain the in-flight rows. Enforced by test_bus_audit_durability (emits 5000 rows through the real producer/consumer, requires exactly 5000 in the real ledger, each once, zero drops). This is a correctness invariant, not a latency budget, but it is committed here because stripping the direct path made it load-bearing.

memory_roundtrip_p50_ns.reason: Audit, not memory, is the first migrated module (memory is not yet modularized). When memory does move onto the bus, its budget is what this file's philosophy says: an ABSOLUTE round-trip ceiling (a reasonable p50/p99 for a request/reply over the bus, filled in here from the migrated module's own measurement) plus a CORRECTNESS invariant (the bus answer is parity-equal to a direct call). It is NOT a factor against a pre-migration in-process baseline — that comparison is explicitly not the budget. Pending until memory migrates.

memory_roundtrip_budget_shape.description: When memory migrates: commit an absolute round-trip ceiling (reasonable-speed p50/p99, like dispatch_overhead_ns and audit_enqueue_overhead_ns) and a parity correctness invariant (bus answer == direct-call answer, like audit_durability's exactly-once). No pre-migration regression factor — correctness plus reasonable absolute speed is the whole budget.
